warning_source: Moshe Davidovich / Confrontation Line Forum, with northern-border mayors
recipient: Yoav Gallant; Bezalel Smotrich; Defense Ministry; Finance Ministry; Netanyahu government; Prime Minister's Office / DG Yossi Shelley
warning_summary: Local leaders warned that cuts and delays in Shield of the North left roughly 250,000 northern-border residents exposed and that Hezbollah understood home-front preparedness to be an Israeli weakness.
evidence_update: Recovered a contemporaneous 22 Mar 2023 publication reproducing Davidovich's urgent letter addressed by name to Defense Minister Yoav Gallant and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich. The letter explicitly described the northern front as sensitive, volatile and dangerous, said 250,000 residents were exposed, and warned that Hezbollah recognized home-front readiness as an Israeli weakness. Defense and Finance Ministry responses were published with it. A separate 6 Jun 2023 report reproduces PMO DG Yossi Shelley correspondence after the PMO requested urgent documents for a government decision. Together these establish direct documented government-level receipt; WARN-64 upgraded from Medium to High without creating a duplicate event.
gaps: No evidence that Gallant or Smotrich personally acted on the letter beyond ministry-level responses; response remains Partially acted. This is a northern civilian-protection/border-vulnerability warning, not an Oct. 7 tactical forecast.

warning_source: Bini Kfir, commander of Moshav Tkuma standby squad
recipient: Unnamed senior Gaza-area officer; previous brigade commander; regional-council heads
warning_summary: Kfir says he repeatedly warned that Tkuma's standby squad could not function after weapons were removed and that a senior officer dismissed the concern because the Gaza barrier eliminated the threat.
evidence_update: Ynet preserves Kfir's retrospective account and the text he says he sent to regional-council heads. A later official IDF History Department study independently corroborates the broader erosion of standby-squad weapons/training and the barrier-driven security conception, but also states there was no authorized blanket order requiring 0–4 km communities to store weapons in armories; written directives generally called for weapons to remain with squad members, while practice varied locally. This materially strengthens structural context while qualifying Kfir's description of an army-wide weapon-removal policy.
gaps: Specific pre-Oct. 7 warning date, named senior recipient and contemporaneous Kfir letter/message remain unrecovered. Same-witness retrospective retellings are not independent event-level corroboration. Keep Investigating.
